# Canonicalization

*Concept* · also written canonicalisation · canonical URL · canonical URLs · canonical

How Google picks one representative URL (the canonical) from a cluster of duplicate pages and indexes that one.

**Glossary** (*Canonical*): The representative URL of a duplicate cluster, the one Google would ideally show; signals such as links are forwarded to it.

Narrative: the topics [Canonical selection](../topics/canonical-selection.md), [Canonical graphs: chains, loops and leaders](../topics/canonical-graphs.md) tell the story; this card lists what links to it.

69 claims mention it: 15 from Google's documentation, 40 shown or said at the event (8 not in Google docs, 5 confirmed by Google docs, 18 consistent with Google docs, 9 nothing to verify), 14 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization), [Fix canonicalization issues](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization-troubleshooting).

- [`D1-C128`](../sessions/D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) Docs: Google's canonicalization guide says some duplicate content on a site is normal and not a violation of its spam policies; Google clusters duplicate pages, picks the most representative one as canonical and crawls the duplicates less often. `[D1-C128, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization]`
- [`D2-C310`](../sessions/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) Docs: Google's canonicalization guide says that when Google indexes a page it determines the page's primary content, which it also calls the centerpiece, and clusters pages whose primary content is the same or very similar. `[D2-C310, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization]`
- [`D2-C357`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Docs: Google's redirects guide says Google keeps track of both the source and the target of a redirect: one becomes the canonical, depending on signals such as whether the redirect is permanent or temporary, and the other becomes an alternate name that may appear in results when a query suggests the user trusts the old URL more. After a move to a new domain, old URLs may still show occasionally; the guide calls this normal. `[D2-C357, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/301-redirects]`
- [`D2-C373`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Docs: Google's canonicalization troubleshooting guide says fixing a wrong duplicate cluster comes down to making the clustered pages sufficiently different; pages split out faster when the difference is clear and significant, and Google may keep pages in a duplicate cluster for up to two weeks after a fix. `[D2-C373, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization-troubleshooting]`
- [`D2-C385`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Docs: Google's canonical guide says that for canonicalization Google prefers URLs that are part of hreflang clusters: if German pages for Germany and Switzerland point to each other with hreflang but not to the Austrian page, the German and Swiss pages are preferred as canonicals. `[D2-C385, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls]`
- [`D2-C391`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Docs: Google's canonical guide ranks the ways to signal a preferred canonical by strength: redirects and rel=canonical annotations are strong signals, sitemap inclusion is a weak signal, and combining methods makes them more effective. `[D2-C391, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls]`
- [`D2-C403`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Docs: Google's guide to specifying canonical URLs says Google supports explicit rel=canonical link annotations as described in RFC 6596, the canonical link relation specification. `[D2-C403, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls]`
- [`D2-C414`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Docs: Google's 2009 Search Central blog post introducing rel=canonical says a canonical URL may be a URL that redirects: Google then processes the redirect as usual. `[D2-C414, docs, Search Central blog (12 February 2009), https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2009/02/specify-your-canonical]`
- [`D2-C418`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Docs: Google's 2013 Search Central blog post on rel=canonical mistakes says to specify no more than one rel=canonical per page: when a page has more than one, Google will likely ignore all of them, and any benefit of a legitimate canonical is lost. `[D2-C418, docs, Search Central blog (8 April 2013), https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2013/04/5-common-mistakes-with-relcanonical]`
- [`D2-C420`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Docs: Google's 2009 Search Central blog post introducing rel=canonical says Google's algorithm is lenient and can follow canonical chains, but strongly recommends updating links to point to a single canonical page for optimal canonicalization. `[D2-C420, docs, Search Central blog (12 February 2009), https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2009/02/specify-your-canonical]`
- [`D2-C430`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Docs: Google's guide to specifying canonical URLs says a canonical helps consolidate signals for duplicate pages: links to a duplicate URL are consolidated with links to the preferred URL once the preferred URL becomes canonical. `[D2-C430, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls]`
- [`D2-C435`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Docs: Google's guide to specifying canonical URLs says that on pages using hreflang, the canonical should be a page in the same language, or the best possible substitute language if no canonical page exists in the same language. `[D2-C435, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls]`
- [`D2-C451`](../sessions/D2-S11-finding-the-gold-nuggets-structured-data-media-and-more.md) Docs: Google's general structured data guidelines recommend placing the same structured data on all duplicate pages of the same content, not just on the canonical page. `[D2-C451, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/sd-policies]`
- [`D2-C702`](../sessions/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) Docs: Google's documentation says a search result usually points to the canonical page, but the other pages in a duplicate cluster are alternate versions that may be served in different contexts, for example a mobile page for a user on a mobile device. `[D2-C702, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization]`
- [`D3-C669`](../sessions/D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) Docs: Google's guide to fixing canonicalization issues says that even after content issues are fixed, Google might hold pages in a duplicate cluster for up to two weeks, and that pages split out faster when they differ clearly and significantly. `[D3-C669, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization-troubleshooting]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D2-C368`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Slide, Day 2, not in Google docs: Google sometimes picks a canonical that looks unrelated because it recognised a URL pattern: if /buy/fax, /buy/typewriter and /office-equipment show the same content, its systems may assume any /buy/ URL, even /buy/seo-service, shows that same office-equipment content without looking at the page. `[D2-C368, slide, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C386`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Google picks the canonical from a variety of criteria and uses some kind of machine learning to decide how much weight each criterion gets; the weighting changes from time to time. `[D2-C386, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C393`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Google's speaker said that pointing rel=canonical from the pages of a paginated set to the first page can sometimes make sense depending on the goal, for example to make a category page more visible, but that it affects canonicalization and deduplication. `[D2-C393, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C421`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Canonical chains can run through canonical links alone, through a server-side redirect between members, or through a client-side redirect between members. `[D2-C421, stage, Tobias Schwarz, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C424`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Canonical loops, such as two HTML pages whose canonical tags point to each other, are a structural conflict: the group has no canonical leader, so its canonical information cannot be used. `[D2-C424, stage, Tobias Schwarz, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C425`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Canonical loops can also run through server-side or client-side redirects, not only through canonical tags. `[D2-C425, stage, Tobias Schwarz, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C426`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: A community speaker said that at best a search engine's heuristic would treat a canonical loop through redirects as self-referencing canonicals, and doubted that this is often done when the loop runs through a client-side redirect. `[D2-C426, stage, Tobias Schwarz, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C429`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: A community speaker said pages carry different link equity, and a canonical leader that is not the strongest page in its group is technically valid but most likely suboptimal for ranking, so the strongest page should be the leader. `[D2-C429, stage, Tobias Schwarz, Day 2]`
- [`D1-C207`](../sessions/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) Stage, Day 1, confirmed by Google docs: Google clusters duplicate pages and selects one page per cluster as its representative, the canonical URL, so that users are not shown duplicates. `[D1-C207, stage, Cherry Prommawin, Day 1]`
- [`D2-C031`](../sessions/D2-S03-how-is-html-interpreted.md) Slide, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: Google extracts the rel=canonical link, through which site owners state their preferred canonical URL, and uses it in deduplication and in canonical selection. `[D2-C031, slide, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C347`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: Google's speaker said what SEOs call the canonical is, for Google, the representative of a cluster of duplicate pages: the URL Google would ideally show. `[D2-C347, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C380`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: Many SEOs assume Google must follow their rel=canonical, but because people sometimes get it wrong, Google has to make its own judgment about the canonical. `[D2-C380, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C438`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: A community speaker advised fixing canonical chains by cleaning up the canonical graph so that every canonical link points directly to the canonical leader. `[D2-C438, stage, Tobias Schwarz, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C359`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Google's duplication talk described three related parts of deduplication: building clusters, localization, and selecting the representative URL, which is the canonicalization site owners see in Search Console. `[D2-C359, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C362`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Whether a redirect is permanent or temporary matters only for choosing the canonical, not for clustering the URLs together. `[D2-C362, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C379`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: rel=canonical is probably the most common way site owners signal duplicates, but it is very often wrong, for example a tag whose value reads 'canonical target' instead of a real URL (the example is partly unclear in the recording), so Google can only sometimes trust it. `[D2-C379, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C388`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Slide, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Google watches for canonical hijacking, where several domains try to be canonical for the same content, whether accidentally across a site owner's own domains (such as a staging copy) or through third-party domains, maliciously or not, and asks site owners to report cases it gets wrong. `[D2-C388, slide, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C389`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Slide, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Whether a page can load is really important for canonical selection: a broken certificate, failing JavaScript or a page that cannot be loaded counts against a URL, and the slide also listed meta refresh and security. `[D2-C389, slide, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C390`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Slide, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Clear site-owner signals about which URL should be canonical make a big difference to Google's choice; the speaker named redirects, listing only the preferred URL in sitemaps, and rel=canonical, which the speaker said also helps a bit. `[D2-C390, slide, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C396`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Slide, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Google's closing suggestions on duplication: use redirects for site migrations, use HTTP result codes, don't block agents, check your rel=canonical links, use hreflang links to help Google localize, report weird canonicals in the forums, make secure pages that work, and keep canonical signals clear. `[D2-C396, slide, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C399`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: When all canonical signals point to the same URL, Google follows what the site owner says; when they point in different directions, Google cannot tell what the owner wants. `[D2-C399, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C417`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Multiple canonical declarations on one page conflict and are invalid, so the search engine applies its own heuristic and picks the canonical for the site owner; a page should declare only one canonical. `[D2-C417, stage, Tobias Schwarz, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C419`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Canonical chains, where a page's canonical target leads on to yet another URL, are named as improper use in the canonical link specification, according to a community speaker. `[D2-C419, stage, Tobias Schwarz, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C422`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Slide, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: The crawler report shown on screen flagged a canonical chain as a problem: canonical links that form a chain instead of all pointing directly to the group's canonical leader. `[D2-C422, slide, Tobias Schwarz, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C427`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: When internal links point only to page A and the canonical leader is reached only through A's canonical link, the leader is reachable by machines but not by human visitors, a signal conflict that asks the search engine to index a page users cannot reach. `[D2-C427, stage, Tobias Schwarz, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C428`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: For a canonical leader that users cannot reach through links, a community speaker suggested revisiting the canonical graph and probably making the internally linked page the leader instead. `[D2-C428, stage, Tobias Schwarz, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C432`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: The canonical leader of a group should be indexable: it should carry no noindex robots directive, return no error status code and not be blocked in robots.txt. `[D2-C432, stage, Tobias Schwarz, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C433`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Canonical links between different language versions of a page are a misuse: if a search engine accepted such a canonical group, only one language version would rank. `[D2-C433, stage, Tobias Schwarz, Day 2]`
- [`D3-C640`](../sessions/D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: A change of canonical URL usually takes one to three weeks to show, though it can happen in seconds because Google allocates enough resources to canonicalization. `[D3-C640, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C641`](../sessions/D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Gary Illyes said he had updated Google's documentation about canonicalization changes about a month before the event (around early September 2026). `[D3-C641, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C642`](../sessions/D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google treats a site move as a complex canonicalization process in which every signal of the old site is recalculated and moved to the new one, and every indexing process has to run. `[D3-C642, stage, Gary Illyes, Day 3]`
- [`D2-C406`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Stage, Day 2, nothing to verify: Checking canonicals pairwise (page A has a canonical to page B, page B a self-referencing canonical) is common but, in a community speaker's experience, misses the bigger picture, such as other links pointing to A or B. `[D2-C406, stage, Tobias Schwarz, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C407`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Stage, Day 2, nothing to verify: In a community speaker's terms, a canonical group is the set of all URLs connected through canonical links, and its canonical leader is the page that all the group's canonical links ultimately point to. `[D2-C407, stage, Tobias Schwarz, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C408`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Stage, Day 2, nothing to verify: A community speaker advised auditing canonicals as whole canonical groups rather than pair by pair, paying special attention to each group's canonical leader. `[D2-C408, stage, Tobias Schwarz, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C409`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Stage, Day 2, nothing to verify: A community speaker said it helps to view small canonical groups as a graph that shows any redirects between members, together with the indexability of each member page. `[D2-C409, stage, Tobias Schwarz, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C410`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Slide, Day 2, nothing to verify: A crawler report shown on screen drew one canonical group of five URLs as a link graph with the leader marked by a crown, and listed each member's HTTP status, indexability, document language, leader flag, incoming and outgoing links, and hints. `[D2-C410, slide, Tobias Schwarz, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C411`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Slide, Day 2, nothing to verify: The crawler report shown on screen ran group-level checks on each canonical group: an overall group status, whether the leader has self links, whether languages are consistent across members, and whether the group contains a chain. `[D2-C411, slide, Tobias Schwarz, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C412`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Slide, Day 2, nothing to verify: In the real-world canonical group shown on screen (a German-language travel magazine section, site not named), a feed URL's canonical pointed to a URL on another subdomain that 301-redirected to the leader, a canonical chain through a server-side redirect. `[D2-C412, slide, Tobias Schwarz, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C413`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Slide, Day 2, nothing to verify: The crawler report shown on screen rated a canonical group member that issues a redirect instead of displaying content as an error, and flagged canonical links whose target returns a non-200 status or is itself a redirect. `[D2-C413, slide, Tobias Schwarz, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C437`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Stage, Day 2, nothing to verify: In a community speaker's experience, real-world canonical graphs are far more complex than the isolated examples in the talk and commonly mix several canonical problems at once. `[D2-C437, stage, Tobias Schwarz, Day 2]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D1-C421`](../sessions/D1-S11-lightning-session-c-crawling.md) Analysis: Of the two answers a community speaker offered for a request to a URL variant (redirect, or an error page), Google's canonicalization guide favours the redirect: a redirect is a strong signal that its target should become canonical, while an error page throws away any links pointing at the variant. `[D1-C421, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D1-C113`](../sessions/D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) Analysis: The real cost of duplicates is control and crawling: Google may choose a canonical you did not want, and every copy is still crawled. Copied or scraped content is a separate spam-policy issue. `[D1-C113, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C363`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Analysis: Use permanent redirects (301 or 308) for moves you want reflected in Search: a temporary redirect still groups the URLs, but it changes which URL Google is likely to pick as the canonical. `[D2-C363, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C372`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Analysis: Make location and variant pages differ in their main content (local stock, staff, prices, addresses) and return 404 for empty or invalid combinations; otherwise every URL that fits the pattern can be folded into one canonical. `[D2-C372, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C392`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Analysis: Google's duplication talk described rel=canonical as something that 'also helps a bit', while Google's canonical guide calls it a strong signal alongside redirects and calls sitemap inclusion weak; treat redirects and rel=canonical as the main levers and sitemaps as support. `[D2-C392, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C394`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Analysis: Google's pagination guide still says not to use page 1 as the canonical of a paginated series, so keep self-referencing canonicals on paginated pages unless you deliberately want later pages folded into page 1 and the items they list are linked from elsewhere. `[D2-C394, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C400`](../sessions/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) Analysis: Before a migration or template change, align every canonical signal for the preferred URL (redirects, rel=canonical, internal links, sitemap entries, hreflang and working HTTPS); Google says it follows the site owner only when the signals agree. `[D2-C400, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C404`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Analysis: A broken canonical setup does not fail visibly: pages still load normally while the choice of URL passes to the search engine's own heuristics, so canonical tags need a regular audit with a crawler and the URL Inspection tool. `[D2-C404, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C431`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Analysis: A leader reachable only through a canonical and a leader with weak link equity share one fix: point internal links, sitemap entries and redirects at the URL chosen as canonical, so the leader is both reachable for users and the strongest page in its group. `[D2-C431, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C436`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Analysis: Check that every canonical group contains a single document language: a group spanning languages means canonicals are joining versions that hreflang should connect, and each language version should keep its own self-referencing canonical. `[D2-C436, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C439`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Analysis: The crawler report shown at the talk rated a redirecting canonical target as an error, while Google's 2009 guidance accepts a canonical URL that redirects and says Google can follow canonical chains; the gap is one of severity, since both recommend pointing every canonical link straight at the final URL. `[D2-C439, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C440`](../sessions/D2-S09-lightning-session-e-managing-duplicates-and-site-moves.md) Analysis: Google says canonicalization consolidates link signals from duplicates into the chosen canonical, so a leader with few links of its own is not necessarily weaker once Google accepts it; the practical risk of a weakly linked leader is that Google, treating rel=canonical as a hint, picks a different page as canonical. `[D2-C440, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C450`](../sessions/D2-S11-finding-the-gold-nuggets-structured-data-media-and-more.md) Analysis: Because Google extracts structured data, images and videos only after deduplication, put markup and media on the URL you want as canonical and keep them identical on its duplicates; markup that exists only on a duplicate that loses canonical selection may never be extracted. `[D2-C450, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D3-C670`](../sessions/D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) Analysis: The canonicalization documentation update mentioned on stage appears in Google's documentation changelog on 10 July 2026 (re-evaluation time, page last updated 21 August 2026), earlier than 'about a month' before the event; its 'up to two weeks' sits at the short end of the one to three weeks said on stage. `[D3-C670, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-CAN-01` **MUST** · Documented: Use permanent server-side redirects (301 or 308) for moved URLs, straight to the final URL (3 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-CAN-02` **MUST** · Documented: Serve one host over HTTPS with a valid certificate and redirect every other origin to it (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-CAN-03` **MUST** · Documented: Put exactly one absolute rel=canonical in the server-rendered head of every indexable page (4 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-CAN-04` **MUST** · Documented: Point every canonical directly at a final URL that returns 200, is indexable and is linked (6 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-CAN-05` **MUST** · Documented: Make all canonical signals agree: redirects, rel=canonical, internal links, sitemaps and hreflang (6 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-CAN-06` **AVOID** · Documented: Do not canonicalise one language version to another; connect them with hreflang (3 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-CAN-07` **AVOID** · Documented: Never leave staging, preview or mirror copies of the site publicly crawlable (1 of its claims mentions it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-CAN-08` **SHOULD** · Documented: Make pages that share a URL pattern differ in their main content (3 of its claims mention it)
- `DEV-MON-06` **SHOULD** · Documented: Audit canonical groups with a crawler on a schedule (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-MON-10` **SHOULD** · Documented: Plan releases and fixes around Google's processing times, and judge results only after them (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-SDA-10` **SHOULD** · Documented: Put the same structured data on duplicate URLs as on the canonical (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-URL-05` **SHOULD** · Documented: Publish XML sitemaps listing only canonical, indexable URLs with accurate lastmod (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-URL-06` **MUST** · Documented: Give each page of a paginated series its own URL, its own canonical and an `<a href>` to the next page (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-URL-09` **SHOULD** · Documented: If facet URLs must be crawlable, use & separators, a fixed filter order and 404 for empty results (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
